candidates.title: Draft updates when order data changes

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing order status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A student can draft from operator-supplied sample order facts; no supplied reference documents status handling.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for clearer status updates; this request establishes neither buyers nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from synthetic status changes; live store access and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed trigger could prepare drafts, but a person must verify changing facts and approve every message.

evidence.reason: The request names customer-facing updates with incomplete or changing data, but gives no frequency or fields.

candidates.reason: Assessed a synthetic-data draft experiment. Rejected below threshold and as a duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6: both serve online shops handling customer communications.

candidates.title: Alert a restaurant when a web order arrives

demandEvidence.chore: Notify an operator when a new restaurant website order arrives.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A student can format a supplied test order into alert text; the source does not document a trigger or delivery tool.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small restaurants may pay for timely order alerts; this request establishes neither buyers nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can format synthetic orders; live website access and message delivery remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can format each supplied order, but a person must verify order details and alert delivery.

evidence.reason: The request seeks an automated restaurant order-notification system, but gives no frequency or workflow details.

candidates.reason: A synthetic-order alert is assessable, but the provisional mean is below 6; no supplied implementation source supports the live order trigger or messaging delivery.

candidates.title: Scheduled order-count check

demandEvidence.chore: Compare order records on a schedule and identify missing, extra, or mismatched orders for a daily email.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The Schedule Trigger started every run itself (one-off cron a few seconds ahead).

ease.reason: A beginner can test sample order rows; n8n documents total and unique counts, but not the comparison or email steps.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service firms handling order records may pay for a daily discrepancy summary; the discussion proves no buyers or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare synthetic rows, while real data mapping and reliable discrepancy rules remain untested.

autonomy.reason: The excerpt confirms a schedule trigger and n8n documents counting inputs; matching exceptions and email delivery are unsupported and need review.

evidence.reason: The title specifies the order-count task and daily email; the excerpt confirms scheduled execution, while docs support counts only.

candidates.reason: Assessed the narrow synthetic-row comparison and daily summary experiment. Below threshold: the reference documents counts, not missing/extra/mismatch detection or email delivery.

rejected.title: Flow-state mouse protocol
rejected.reason: The excerpt describes a self-built biohacking protocol for entering flow, not a concrete existing professional chore suitable for a bounded AI service. No implementation reference is assigned.

rejected.title: Freelance workflow-building offer
rejected.reason: The excerpt lists a freelancer’s integration skills but states no specific client task or request. Inferring duties from the service categories would invent demand.

rejected.title: Voicebots for sales
rejected.reason: The excerpt says voicebots still cannot be used in sales, but identifies no concrete manual task, workflow or bounded deliverable; proposing one would invent the chore.

rejected.title: Scheduled order-count check
rejected.reason: Below threshold after five-criterion assessment: a mock could compare synthetic rows, but supplied evidence supports scheduled execution and counts only, not discrepancy detection or email delivery.

rejected.title: Travel and shopping research apps
rejected.reason: The question asks whether specialized apps are needed but describes no concrete repeated research task, buyer or decision process.

rejected.title: Private support-ticket access problem
rejected.reason: This is a one-off access problem phrased as a support question, not evidence of a recurring customer chore; automating access to private tickets is unsupported.

steps.message: Preserved the seven original assessments and exclusions, then assessed the omitted scheduled order-count chore. Its synthetic comparison experiment remains below threshold because the supplied implementation reference documents counts only; no post qualifies.
